mainTopic: The closing משנה of תענית (tragedies, mourning in אב, the joy of ט״ו באב) and the גמרא on ברכת כהנים at fast-day תפילות
overview: This amud finishes the last משנה of מסכת תענית and begins its גמרא. The משנה completes the five tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז and lists the five tragedies of תשעה באב. It then gives the stages of mourning: less joy from the start of אב, no haircuts or laundry in the week of תשעה באב, and a simple meal on ערב תשעה באב. The מסכתא ends with joy: on ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים the girls of ירושלים went out in borrowed white clothes and urged the young men to choose a wife for family and יראת שמים. The גמרא then goes back to an earlier line of the משנה about ברכת כהנים four times a day and fixes its wording. It brings a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבי יוסי about ברכת כהנים at מנחה and נעילה, which all turns on the worry about drunkenness. The final ruling follows רבי יוסי, and a late מנחה on a fast day is treated like נעילה. Last, the גמרא finds the source that a drunk כהן may not bless: the כהן who blesses is compared to the כהן who serves in the מקדש.

steps.title: Finishing the list of the five tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז
steps.stepSummary: The משנה completes its list of five tragedies that happened on שבעה עשר בתמוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: The tablets were broken, the daily offering stopped, the city wall was breached, אפוסטמוס burned the תורה, and an idol was placed in the Sanctuary (by מנשה, according to רש״י).
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a list it began on the previous amud: five sad events that happened on שבעה עשר בתמוז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list explains why שבעה עשר בתמוז is a fast day. Each item is a separate disaster, from the time of משה רבינו (the broken לוחות) through the Roman era (the end of the תמיד and the breach of the walls).

keyTerms.meaning: The Tablets of the Covenant, which משה broke after the golden calf
The daily communal offering brought in the בית המקדש
Was breached (the city walls were broken through)
An idol or image
The Sanctuary of the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins mid-sentence. The heading 'five things happened on שבעה עשר בתמוז' came right before it. These five events belong to the 17th of תמוז, not to תשעה באב.

phrases.english: The tablets were broken,
and the daily offering was stopped,
and the city (wall) was breached,
and Apostemos burned the Torah,
and he placed an idol in the Sanctuary.
phrases.notes: The גמרא later debates who placed the idol.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a list begun in the preceding text of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five tragedies occurred on שבעה עשר בתמוז.

steps.title: The five tragedies of תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists five tragedies that happened on תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: On תשעה באב it was decreed that our fathers would not enter ארץ ישראל. The בית המקדש was destroyed both the first and second time, ביתר was captured, and the city was plowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a parallel list of five disasters that happened on תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first tragedy goes back to the מרגלים in the desert, when the generation was told it would not enter ארץ ישראל. The rest are national catastrophes: both בתי המקדש, the fall of ביתר, and the plowing of ירושלים. This list explains why תשעה באב is the most serious fast.

keyTerms.meaning: It was decreed
The House, meaning the בית המקדש
The city that fell in the בר כוכבא revolt
Was plowed over

phrases.english: On the Ninth of Av it was decreed upon our fathers
that they would not enter the Land,
and the Temple was destroyed the first time and the second time,
and Beitar was captured, and the city was plowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel list, moving from the 17th of תמוז to תשעה באב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five tragedies occurred on תשעה באב.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two parallel lists of five tragedies. One is for שבעה עשר בתמוז and one is for תשעה באב.

steps.title: Reducing joy once אב begins
steps.stepSummary: From the start of the month of אב, we cut back on joyful activities.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once אב begins, we reduce our rejoicing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns from history to practical law. It starts with the first stage of mourning: reducing joy from ראש חודש אב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the widest and mildest layer of mourning. It does not forbid anything specific, but it sets a general mood of less celebration. The next steps will add stricter rules as the fast gets closer.

keyTerms.meaning: From when the month of אב begins
We reduce rejoicing

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the familiar תשעת הימים, the period of reduced celebration.

phrases.english: From when Av begins, we reduce rejoicing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the tragedies of תשעה באב to the mourning practices tied to it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Joy is reduced from the beginning of אב.

steps.title: No haircuts or laundering in the week of תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: In the week that contains תשעה באב, cutting hair and laundering are forbidden, but on Thursday they are allowed out of respect for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the week in which תשעה באב falls, it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder. But on Thursday these are permitted, out of respect for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a stricter second layer of mourning that applies only in the week of תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'שבת' means the week, not the day of rest. Haircuts and washing clothes are forbidden that week. The Thursday exception exists so a person can get ready for שבת. The משנה does not spell out here which case this is.

keyTerms.meaning: The week in which (the day) falls
To cut hair
To launder clothes
Honor of שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The word שבת here means 'the week', not Saturday. Read it as 'the week in which תשעה באב falls'.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ
phrases.english: The week in which the Ninth of Av falls
it is forbidden to cut hair and to launder,
but on Thursday they are permitted because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁבָּת שֶׁחָל תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לִהְיוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter layer of mourning closer to the fast
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Haircuts and laundering are forbidden in the week of תשעה באב, with a Thursday exception for כבוד שבת.

steps.title: The limited meal on ערב תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: On ערב תשעה באב, a person may not eat two cooked dishes, meat, or wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב תשעה באב, a person may not eat two cooked dishes. He may not eat meat and may not drink wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the strictest layer before the fast itself: limits on the last meal before תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat and wine are signs of celebration, and two cooked dishes are a sign of a full feast. The last meal must be simple, like that of a mourner. This is the anonymous first opinion (the תנא קמא), and dissenting views follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The eve, the day before
Cooked dishes
Meat
Wine

phrases.english: On the eve of the Ninth of Av
a person may not eat two cooked dishes,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר וְלֹא יִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן.
phrases.english: he may not eat meat and may not drink wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next stage of mourning, now on the day right before the fast
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The meal before תשעה באב excludes two cooked dishes, meat, and wine.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: one should change his usual eating
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a different approach. A person should change (reduce) his normal eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: He should change.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion appears in the משנה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says only 'he should change' from his regular eating habits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a fixed list of banned foods, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a personal standard. Each person cuts back compared to what he normally eats. The גמרא will later explain exactly what 'change' means.

keyTerms.meaning: He should change (his usual practice)

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: יְשַׁנֶּה.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: He should change.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: יְשַׁנֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Dissenting or alternative view on the pre-fast meal
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should reduce his eating compared to his usual habit.

steps.title: רבי יהודה requires overturning the bed, but the Sages disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה requires overturning the bed as mourners do, but the חכמים reject this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה obligates overturning the bed, but the חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion appears. רבי יהודה would add a mourner's practice, overturning the bed, but the חכמים rule against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Overturning the bed (כפיית המטה) is a practice of a personal mourner. רבי יהודה wants to treat תשעה באב the same way. The phrase 'the חכמים did not agree with him' tells us the הלכה does not follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Overturning the bed, a mourner's practice
Obligates
The Sages did not agree with him

steps.whatToRemember: The mourning builds in stages: reduced joy from ראש חודש אב, no haircuts or laundry that week, and a simple meal on ערב תשעה באב. The חכמים do not require overturning the bed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda obligates overturning the bed,
but the Sages did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further, stricter view on mourning practices, which the חכמים reject
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה requires overturning the bed. The חכמים do not.

steps.title: The great joy of ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says there were no happier days than ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים. On those days the girls of ירושלים went out in borrowed white clothes, so as not to embarrass those who had none.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: There were no days as joyous for ישראל as ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים. On them the daughters of ירושלים would go out in borrowed white garments, so as not to embarrass anyone who did not have her own.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה switches from sadness to joy so that the מסכתא can end on a happy note. It describes the festive days of ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every girl wore borrowed clothing, even a girl who owned nice clothes. That way nobody could tell who was poor. The joy of the day was built around protecting other people's dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: Joyous days, festive days
The Fifteenth of אב
White garments
Borrowed
To embarrass

steps.confusionAlert: Here כלים means clothing, not utensils or vessels.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ends the מסכתא of fasts and tragedy with a picture of joy and sensitivity to others.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
There were no days as joyous for Israel
as the Fifteenth of Av and as Yom Kippur,
for on them the daughters of Jerusalem would go out
in borrowed white garments —

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְבַיֵּישׁ אֶת מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ.
phrases.english: so as not to embarrass one who does not have (her own).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: לֹא הָיוּ יָמִים טוֹבִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the mourning of אב to the joy of ט״ו באב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים were the most joyous days, marked by borrowed white clothing.

steps.title: All the borrowed garments require immersion
steps.stepSummary: All the borrowed garments had to be immersed in a מקוה before being worn.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the garments require immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a detail about the borrowed clothes: each one needed טבילה before use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous wearer might have been טמא, so the garment might be טמא. Immersing every garment made sure each one was טהור before it was worn.

keyTerms.meaning: Require
Immersion in a מקוה

steps.whatToRemember: The מסכתא closes with ט״ו באב: borrowed white garments, each immersed first, worn so that no girl would be embarrassed.

phrases.english: All the garments require immersion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a purity detail to the borrowed-garments practice

steps.title: The girls dance in the vineyards and call out to the young men
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the girls of ירושלים dancing in the vineyards and telling the young men to pick a wife based on family and יראת שמים, not beauty, backed by two פסוקים from משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The girls of ירושלים would go out and dance in the vineyards. What would they say? 'Young man, lift up your eyes and see whom you are choosing for yourself. Do not look at beauty. Look at family. As the פסוק says: "Grace is false and beauty is empty; a woman who fears ה׳, she is the one to be praised." And it says: "Give her from the fruit of her hands, and let her deeds praise her in the gates."'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps describing what happened on ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים. The girls danced and gave the young men advice about choosing a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the girls all wore borrowed white clothes, so nobody would stand out by wealth. Here the same idea continues: look past the outside (beauty) to what really counts (family and יראת שמים). The two פסוקים from משלי back this up: charm fades, but a God-fearing woman and her good deeds earn true praise.

keyTerms.meaning: Vineyards. This is where the girls went out to dance.
Young man.
Beauty, outward looks.
Family, a good family background.
Fear of God, real יראת שמים.

phrases.english: And the daughters of Jerusalem would go out
and dance in the vineyards.
And what would they say?
Young man, please lift up your eyes
and see what you are choosing for yourself.
phrases.notes: That is, which wife you choose.

phrases.english: Do not set your eyes on beauty;
set your eyes on family.
"Grace is false and beauty is empty,
a woman who fears the Lord, she shall be praised";
and it says: "Give her from the fruit of her hands,
and let her deeds praise her in the gates."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the joyful days begun in steps 8 and 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ט״ו באב and יום הכפורים the girls danced and urged the young men to choose a wife for her family and יראת שמים rather than her beauty.

steps.title: A פסוק from שיר השירים about the wedding day and the joyful day
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a פסוק from שיר השירים and explains it: 'the day of his wedding' is מתן תורה, and 'the day of the joy of his heart' is the building of the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so the פסוק says: "Go out and see, daughters of ציון, King שלמה, with the crown his mother crowned him with on the day of his wedding and on the day of the joy of his heart." 'The day of his wedding' means מתן תורה. 'The day of the joy of his heart' means the building of the בית המקדש, may it be rebuilt quickly in our days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes its description with a פסוק that hints at why these days are so happy. It then explains what the two parts of the פסוק stand for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'King שלמה' here is read as a reference to הקב״ה, the King of peace. His 'wedding day' with כלל ישראל is מתן תורה, which links to יום הכפורים, the day the second לוחות were given. 'The joy of his heart' is the בית המקדש, so the משנה ends with a prayer that it be rebuilt soon.

keyTerms.meaning: Daughters of ציון. This echoes the daughters of ירושלים who went out to dance.
His wedding.
The giving of the תורה.
The building of the בית המקדש.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends the מסכת's description of joy by tying יום הכפורים to מתן תורה (the second לוחות). The great joy of that day comes from its closeness to הקב״ה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how יום הכפורים, a fast day, can be called one of the happiest days of the year. It is the day of forgiveness and of receiving the תורה again.

phrases.english: And so it says:
"Go out and see, daughters of Zion,
King Solomon,
phrases.notes: Read here as הקב״ה, the King of peace.

phrases.english: with the crown with which his mother crowned him
on the day of his wedding
and on the day of the joy of his heart."
"On the day of his wedding": this is the giving of the Torah,
phrases.notes: The second לוחות were given on יום הכפורים.

phrases.aramaic: ״וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַת לִבּוֹ״ — זֶה בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: "and on the day of the joy of his heart": this is the building of the Temple,
may it be built speedily in our days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a פסוק that supports the theme of the joyful days and explains it through a דרשה.
steps.raayaObject: That these days, especially יום הכפורים, are days of great joy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים 3:11, read as referring to מתן תורה and the בית המקדש.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the כהנים raising their hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by quoting the line of the משנה about כהנים doing נשיאת כפים at three times of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'At three times in the year, the כהנים raise their hands (to bless the people)...' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by quoting a line from the משנה that it wants to discuss. This step is setting up a question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the פרק (on 26a), the משנה said that at three times a year the כהנים do ברכת כהנים four times in one day. The גמרא brings back that line now because it is about to point out a problem with it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים on the משנה.
Times or occasions (here, of the year).
Raise their hands, meaning they recite ברכת כהנים.
Etc. The quote continues in the משנה.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
At three times in the year
the priests raise their hands, etc.
phrases.notes: The full משנה says: four times a day, on fast days, מעמדות, and יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּרָקִים בַּשָּׁנָה כֹּהֲנִים נוֹשְׂאִין אֶת כַּפֵּיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the narrative ending of the משנה and opens the גמרא on an earlier line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה states that on three occasions the כהנים raise their hands four times in a day.

steps.title: Fast days and מעמדות have no מוסף
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how there can be four rounds of ברכת כהנים on fast days and מעמדות, since those days have no מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do fast days and מעמדות have a מוסף?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the wording of the משנה. Four blessings would need four תפילות, but fast days and מעמדות do not have a מוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four תפילות the משנה has in mind are שחרית, מוסף, מנחה and נעילה. Only יום הכפורים has a מוסף. An ordinary fast day or a gathering of the מעמד has no extra קרבן, so it has no מוסף. So it seems impossible for all three occasions to have four blessings.

keyTerms.meaning: Public fast days.
Groups of ordinary Jews (not כהנים) who stood as representatives of the people during their משמר's week of service in the בית המקדש.
The extra תפילה said on days that had a קרבן מוסף.
Is there...?! A rhetorical question meaning 'surely there is not.'

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'מי' here does not mean 'who.' In Aramaic, מי at the start of a question means 'Is it so that...?' and works as a challenge.

phrases.english: Fast days and non-priestly watches:
is there a מוסף on them?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that on all three occasions the כהנים bless four times a day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Four blessings need four תפילות, including מוסף. Fast days and מעמדות have no מוסף, so they cannot have four blessings.

steps.title: Words are missing from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing words. On all three occasions the כהנים bless at every תפילה, and only some of those days have four תפילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Words are missing from the משנה, and this is what it means: At three times the כהנים raise their hands every time the people daven. Some of these days have four times a day: שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילת שערים. And these are the three times: fast days, מעמדות, and יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by saying the משנה left some words out. It then gives the full, corrected reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main rule is now that on these three occasions the כהנים bless at every תפילה of the day. The number 'four' applies only to 'some of them,' meaning יום הכפורים, which has מוסף. Fast days and מעמדות get ברכת כהנים at each of their three תפילות.

keyTerms.meaning: Something is missing (from the משנה), so it must be read with added words.
And this is what it teaches.
That they daven.
The closing of the gates: the נעילה תפילה.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think all three occasions have four blessings. Only 'some of them' (יום הכפורים) have four. The others have ברכת כהנים at each of their three תפילות.

phrases.english: It is incomplete,
and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּרָקִים כֹּהֲנִים נוֹשְׂאִין אֶת כַּפֵּיהֶן
phrases.english: At three times the priests raise their hands
every time that they pray,
and some of them have four times a day:
morning prayer and additional prayer,
afternoon prayer and the closing of the gates;
and these are the three times:
fast days, non-priestly watches, and Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by reading the משנה as missing words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מיחסרא: rereading the משנה with words added
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three occasions have four rounds of ברכת כהנים, which cannot work for days without מוסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: On all three occasions the כהנים bless at every תפילה. Only יום הכפורים, which has מוסף, reaches four.

steps.title: This is רבי מאיר's view; the חכמים limit it to שחרית and מוסף
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says the משנה follows רבי מאיר. The חכמים say נשיאת כפים is done at שחרית and מוסף but not at מנחה or נעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: This is the view of רבי מאיר. But the חכמים say: שחרית and מוסף have נשיאת כפים; מנחה and נעילה do not have נשיאת כפים.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא tells us whose opinion the משנה follows. He adds that the חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after the fix in step 14, the משנה still has ברכת כהנים at מנחה and נעילה. רב נחמן says that this is only רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים hold that ברכת כהנים is said only at the morning תפילות (שחרית and מוסף). Steps 19-22 explain why the later תפילות are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who reports this teaching.
רב נחמן's teacher, whom he quotes.
This is the view of רבי מאיר.
Raising of the hands: ברכת כהנים.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and the חכמים about נשיאת כפים at מנחה and נעילה. The rest of the סוגיא, and the practical הלכה, are built on it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.
But the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: שַׁחֲרִית וּמוּסָף — יֵשׁ בָּהֶן נְשִׂיאַת כַּפַּיִם,
phrases.english: The morning prayer and the additional prayer have the raising of the hands,

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחָה וּנְעִילָה — אֵין בָּהֶן נְשִׂיאַת כַּפַּיִם.
phrases.english: the afternoon prayer and the closing prayer do not have the raising of the hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה's reading is settled, identifies it as רבי מאיר's view and presents the opposing view of the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who requires נשיאת כפים at every תפילה. The חכמים allow it only at שחרית and מוסף, not at מנחה and נעילה.

steps.title: Who are the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is meant by the 'חכמים' who disagree with רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are these חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which specific רבי is meant by the 'חכמים' mentioned in the previous step. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said the חכמים allow נשיאת כפים only at שחרית and מוסף. 'חכמים' is an unnamed group. The גמרא wants to give a name to that opinion so we can find its source.

keyTerms.meaning: Who?
The Sages; often an unnamed majority view

phrases.english: Who are the Sages?
phrases.notes: Refers back to the חכמים in the statement of רב נחמן (Step 15).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the unnamed חכמים mentioned in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא behind the 'חכמים' position.

steps.title: The חכמים are רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'חכמים' view is the opinion of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'חכמים' are really רבי יהודה. The source for this comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An opinion called 'חכמים' in one place can match a named תנא in a ברייתא. Here the view that only שחרית and מוסף get נשיאת כפים is exactly what רבי יהודה says.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view matches the 'חכמים'

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.

steps.title: The ברייתא with three opinions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records three views: רבי מאיר (all four תפילות), רבי יהודה (only שחרית and מוסף), and רבי יוסי (נעילה yes, מנחה no).
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילה all have נשיאת כפים. This is the view of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: שחרית and מוסף have נשיאת כפים, but מנחה and נעילה do not. רבי יוסי says: נעילה has נשיאת כפים, but מנחה does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the 'חכמים' view belongs to רבי יהודה. The ברייתא also adds a third view, from רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's view matches the משנה, which allows ברכת כהנים at every תפילה. רבי יהודה's view matches the 'חכמים', so the identification is proven. רבי יוסי takes a middle position: נעילה gets ברכת כהנים, but מנחה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Raising of the hands; ברכת כהנים
The closing תפילה said on יום כיפור and on certain fast days
A third תנא with a middle view

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'middle' opinions. רבי יהודה puts מנחה and נעילה together (both out). רבי יוסי splits them (נעילה in, מנחה out).

phrases.english: As it is taught: the morning prayer, the additional prayer, the afternoon prayer, and ne'ila
all of them have the raising of the hands,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says: the morning prayer and the additional prayer
have the raising of the hands,

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחָה וּנְעִילָה — אֵין בָּהֶן נְשִׂיאַת כַּפַּיִם.
phrases.english: the afternoon prayer and ne'ila do not have the raising of the hands.
Rabbi Yosei says: ne'ila
has the raising of the hands,
the afternoon prayer does not have the raising of the hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source proving the answer of Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'חכמים' view (only שחרית and מוסף) is רבי יהודה's.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the views of רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבי יוסי.

steps.title: What is the basis of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what underlying idea divides the three תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind each of the three opinions. This question sets up the next three steps, one for each תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing what each תנא rules is not enough. The גמרא wants the principle that leads each one to his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asks for the root of a מחלוקת)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from what the ברייתא says to why each view holds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reasoning that separates רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: no drunkenness on a fast day
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that the only reason to skip ברכת כהנים at מנחה is drunkenness. On a fast day nobody drinks, so all four תפילות get it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: what is the reason that every day the כהנים do not spread their hands at מנחה? Because of drunkenness. Today, on a fast day, there is no drunkenness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי מאיר's view. On a normal day, כהנים skip מנחה because they may have drunk wine at lunch. On a fast day no one eats or drinks, so that reason does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A drunk כהן may not give ברכת כהנים. For רבי מאיר the rule simply follows its reason: no wine means no problem. So מנחה and נעילה on a fast day get ברכת כהנים too.

keyTerms.meaning: Drunkenness
Spread their hands; give ברכת כהנים
Now; here, on the fast day

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
every day, what is the reason
that the priests do not spread their hands at the afternoon prayer?
Because of drunkenness;
now there is no drunkenness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of three answers to Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The concern is drunkenness, and on a fast day there is none, so every תפילה gets נשיאת כפים.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the Rabbis' rule stays in place
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that the Rabbis made a fixed rule for the afternoon-time תפילות, which are times when drunkenness is common. That rule applies even on a fast day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: at שחרית and מוסף, which every day are not times of common drunkenness, the Rabbis did not make a decree. At מנחה and נעילה, which every day are times of common drunkenness, the Rabbis made a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יהודה's view. The Rabbis made a decree against ברכת כהנים at the later תפילות of the day, and that decree does not switch off on a fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה does not just check whether there is drunkenness today. Once the Rabbis made a גזירה for the afternoon תפילות, it stays in force even when its reason is missing. נעילה is treated like מנחה because both are said late in the day.

keyTerms.meaning: Common; frequent
The Rabbis made a decree (גזירה)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה agrees there is no drunkenness on a fast day. He holds back ברכת כהנים only because of the general rabbinic decree, not because of any real worry that the כהן is drunk today.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
the morning and additional prayers, which on every day
drunkenness is not common,
the Rabbis did not decree concerning them;
the afternoon prayer and ne'ila, which on every day
drunkenness is common,
the Rabbis decreed concerning them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's reasoning, in contrast to רבי מאיר's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Rabbis' decree covers the times of day when drunkenness is common (מנחה and נעילה), and it applies even on a fast day.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the decree covers only the daily מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that the decree applies to מנחה, which is said every day. It does not apply to נעילה, which is not said every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds: מנחה, which is said every day, the Rabbis decreed about it. נעילה, which is not said every day, the Rabbis did not decree about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוסי's view. The decree follows the daily מנחה even on a fast day, but it does not reach נעילה, which is a special תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי agrees the decree stays in force on a fast day. But he limits it to a תפילה said every day. Since נעילה is rare, no one will confuse it with an ordinary day's מנחה, so there was no need to include it in the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Which exists; which is said
Which does not exist; which is not said

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on ברכת כהנים at the later תפילות of a fast day. רבי מאיר: the reason is drunkenness, and there is none today, so all four get it. רבי יהודה: the Rabbis' decree for the late-day תפילות stands, so only שחרית and מוסף get it. רבי יוסי: the decree covers only the daily מנחה, so נעילה gets it and מנחה does not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds:
the afternoon prayer, which exists every day,
the Rabbis decreed concerning it;
ne'ila, which does not exist every day,
the Rabbis did not decree concerning it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third reasoning, which narrows רבי יהודה's decree to the daily מנחה only.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree applies only to a תפילה said every day (מנחה), not to the rare נעילה.

steps.title: Three אמוראים rule in favor of רבי מאיר, each in different words
steps.stepSummary: רב rules הלכה כרבי מאיר. רבי יוחנן says נהגו העם כרבי מאיר. רבא says מנהג כרבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר. And רבי יוחנן said: The people practice like רבי מאיר. And רבא said: The custom follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the three תנאים have been explained, the גמרא brings three אמוראים who all side with רבי מאיר (ברכת כהנים at all four תפילות of a fast day). Each one uses different wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three agree with רבי מאיר, but their wording differs: 'הלכה', 'נהגו העם', and 'מנהג'. Those different words mean different levels of strength. The next step explains exactly what each one means.

keyTerms.meaning: The binding law
The people practice this way (on their own)
An accepted custom

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these three אמוראים are saying the same thing in different words. The גמרא will show that each phrase has a different practical meaning.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
The halacha follows Rabbi Meir.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
The people practice like Rabbi Meir.
And Rava said:
The custom follows Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the three views to ruling between them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three אמוראים side with רבי מאיר, using three different levels of wording: הלכה, נהגו העם, and מנהג.

steps.title: The practical difference between הלכה, מנהג, and נהגו
steps.stepSummary: 'הלכה' is taught publicly. 'מנהג' is not taught publicly, but a רב tells someone who asks. 'נהגו' is not even told to someone who asks, but if he did it, we do not make him repeat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'the הלכה follows רבי מאיר' means we teach it in the public lecture. The one who says 'custom' means we do not teach it publicly, but we do rule that way when asked. And the one who says 'they practice' means we do not even rule that way when asked, but if someone did it, it is done, and we do not make him go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what each of the three wordings from the last step means in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels. 'הלכה' is the strongest: announced in public. 'מנהג' is in the middle: not announced, but a רב answers that way in private. 'נהגו' is the weakest: a רב does not tell people to do it, but if someone already did it, his action is valid after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: We teach it in the public lecture
We give a ruling (when someone asks)
We do not make him go back and redo it

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels of strength: הלכה (taught publicly) is stronger than מנהג (ruled privately when asked), which is stronger than נהגו (only valid after the fact).
steps.whyThisMatters: This three-level scale of הלכה, מנהג, and נהגו is a basic tool used throughout ש״ס to measure how strong a ruling is.

phrases.english: The one who said 'the halacha follows Rabbi Meir' —
means we teach it in the public lecture.
The one who said 'custom' —
means we do not teach it publicly,
but we do rule that way (when asked).
And the one who said 'they practice' —
means we do not even rule that way (when asked),
but if he did it, it is done,
phrases.notes: His action is valid after the fact.

phrases.english: and we do not make him go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר — דָּרְשִׁינַן לַהּ בְּפִירְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the three wordings used in Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלכה is taught publicly. מנהג is ruled privately when someone asks. נהגו is not ruled at all, but it is valid after the fact.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees with the others and rules like רבי יוסי: ברכת כהנים at נעילה, but not at מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth אמורא gives a different ruling: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, not רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי (Step 22), the decree against ברכת כהנים at מנחה applies even on a fast day, because מנחה is said every day. נעילה is not said every day, so it does get ברכת כהנים. רב נחמן adopts this middle position.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who rules here like רבי יוסי

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing ruling to the three אמוראים in Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: ברכת כהנים at נעילה, but not at מנחה of a fast day.

steps.title: The final ruling follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא decides: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא itself gives the final decision: we rule like רבי יוסי, as רב נחמן said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though three אמוראים leaned toward רבי מאיר, the final ruling is like רבי יוסי. So at מנחה of a fast day, there should be no ברכת כהנים. That creates a problem with what people actually do, which the next step raises.

keyTerms.meaning: And the (final) law is

steps.whatToRemember: Final ruling: like רבי יוסי. There is ברכת כהנים at נעילה, but not at מנחה.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides in favor of רב נחמן's ruling.

steps.title: Why do כהנים bless at מנחה of a fast day nowadays?
steps.stepSummary: If the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, why do כהנים nowadays bless at מנחה of a fast day?
steps.simpleTranslation: And nowadays, what is the reason that the כהנים spread their hands (to bless) at מנחה of a fast day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that real-life practice seems to contradict the ruling it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says there is no ברכת כהנים at מנחה, even on a fast day. Yet people actually see the כהנים blessing at מנחה of a fast day. So either the ruling or the practice seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Nowadays
The כהנים spread their hands (to bless)
מנחה of a fast day

phrases.english: And nowadays, what is the reason
that the Kohanim spread their hands
at the Mincha prayer of a fast day?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִידָּנָא מַאי טַעְמָא פָּרְשִׂי כָּהֲנֵי יְדַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 26 from current practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling like רבי יוסי (no ברכת כהנים at מנחה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Current practice has ברכת כהנים at מנחה of a fast day, which seems to go against רבי יוסי.

steps.title: מנחה close to sunset is treated like נעילה
steps.stepSummary: Because that מנחה is said close to sunset, it is treated like נעילה, so the decree does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they spread their hands close to sunset, it is like the נעילה prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the practice does fit רבי יוסי, because this late מנחה counts like נעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי only banned ברכת כהנים at the everyday-type מנחה. The fast-day מנחה is said very late, close to sunset, so it looks like נעילה, which רבי יוסי allows. The ruling stays the same. Only the way it is applied to this late מנחה is explained.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunset
The closing prayer, said near sunset on certain fast days
It is similar to / treated like

steps.confusionAlert: This late מנחה is still מנחה. It is only treated like נעילה for ברכת כהנים because of its timing.

phrases.english: Since close to sunset
they spread (their hands) —
it is like the Neilah prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּבְסָמוּךְ לִשְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה קָא פָּרְשִׂי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the case: late מנחה is treated like נעילה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blessing at fast-day מנחה goes against רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because it is close to sunset, this מנחה is treated like נעילה, which רבי יוסי allows.

steps.title: Everyone agrees a drunk כהן may not bless
steps.stepSummary: Whatever the מחלוקת, all three תנאים agree that a drunk כהן is forbidden to do ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, everyone agrees that a drunk person is forbidden to raise his hands (for ברכת כהנים).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls out a point that all the opinions share: a drunk כהן may not bless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole debate was about whether the fear of drunkenness should cancel ברכת כהנים at certain times. All sides assume that real drunkenness does disqualify a כהן. This shared basic rule now needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone
In any event / at least
A drunk person
Raising the hands, meaning ברכת כהנים

phrases.english: In any event, according to everyone,
a drunk person is forbidden to raise his hands (to bless).

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת שִׁכּוֹר אָסוּר בִּנְשִׂיאַת כַּפַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pulls a shared principle out of the three views.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All agree that a drunk כהן may not do ברכת כהנים.

steps.title: What is the source for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a drunk כהן may not bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule in the last step. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for a source, not an attack. The rule is accepted, and the גמרא wants to know which פסוק or teaching it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of Step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a drunk כהן may not do ברכת כהנים.

steps.title: Learned from ברכת כהנים being placed next to נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי, quoting בר קפרא: the פרשה of ברכת כהנים comes right after the פרשה of נזיר. This teaches that just as a נזיר may not drink wine, a כהן who blesses may not drink wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said in the name of בר קפרא: Why is the section of the כהן who blesses placed next to the section of the נזיר? To say: just as a נזיר is forbidden in wine, so too a כהן who blesses is forbidden in wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source: the Torah places ברכת כהנים right next to the laws of נזיר, and that placement teaches the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In במדבר chapter 6, the laws of נזיר are followed right away by ברכת כהנים. Placing two sections side by side (סמיכות פרשיות) shows they share a law. So the ban on wine for a נזיר carries over to a כהן while he blesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Was placed next to
The Torah section of
A כהן who gives the blessing
A נזיר, who is forbidden to drink wine

steps.whatToRemember: A drunk כהן may not bless. The source is that ברכת כהנים is placed right next to the פרשה of נזיר: just as a נזיר may not drink wine, neither may the blessing כהן.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of bar Kappara:
Why is the section of the blessing Kohen placed
next to the section of the nazir?
To say: just as a nazir is forbidden in wine,
so too a Kohen who blesses is forbidden in wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִסְמְכָה פָּרָשַׁת כֹּהֵן מְבָרֵךְ לְפָרָשַׁת נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From סמיכות פרשיות: ברכת כהנים comes next to נזיר, so just as a נזיר may not drink wine, neither may the blessing כהן.

steps.title: If the כהן is compared to a נזיר, he should be forbidden to eat grape pits too
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דרבי זירא, or some say אושעיא בר זבדא, attacks the comparison to נזיר. A נזיר is forbidden even in grape pits, so a blessing כהן would also have to be forbidden in grape pits. That result is clearly unacceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא's father challenged this, and some say it was אושעיא בר זבדא: If so, just as a נזיר is forbidden to eat grape pits, a כהן who blesses should also be forbidden to eat grape pits!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source it just gave (the comparison to נזיר). It shows that the comparison proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison usually carries over all the rules of one case to the other. A נזיר is forbidden in every grape product, even the pits. So if the blessing כהן is fully like a נזיר, he could not eat grape pits before blessing, and nobody holds that.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly challenged it. This is a strong objection formula.
And some say. It gives a second version of who said it.
A person who took a vow to avoid all grape products, haircuts, and contact with the dead
Grape pits or seeds. A נזיר is forbidden to eat them.
If just as... so too. This formula pushes a comparison to its full result.

steps.confusionAlert: The challenger is not saying the כהן really is forbidden in grape pits. He is saying the comparison to נזיר must be wrong, or at least incomplete, because it leads to that absurd result.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira's father strongly objected to it,
and some say it was Oshaya bar Zavda:
phrases.notes: Two versions of who raised the challenge

phrases.english: If so, just as a nazir is forbidden in grape pits,
so too a blessing kohen should be forbidden in grape pits!
phrases.notes: An absurd result, which shows the comparison is a problem

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It attacks the נזיר comparison given in step 31 as the source for the drunk-כהן rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר קפרא's derivation that the blessing כהן is like a נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would also carry over the נזיר's ban on grape pits, which is clearly not the halacha for a כהן.

steps.title: The verse compares the blessing כהן to the serving כהן, who may eat grape pits
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק brings the verse "לשרתו ולברך בשמו." It puts blessing next to serving in the מקדש. A serving כהן is allowed grape pits, so a blessing כהן is also allowed grape pits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: The verse says, "To serve Him and to bless in His name." Just as one who serves is allowed grape pits, so too a כהן who blesses is allowed grape pits.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the challenge with a verse. The verse compares the blessing כהן to the כהן who serves in the מקדש, not to a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן who serves in the מקדש may not serve after drinking wine, but he is allowed to eat grape pits. Because the verse joins "serving" and "blessing," the blessing כהן gets the serving כהן's rules. So he may not bless drunk, but grape pits are fine. This avoids the problem that came from comparing him fully to a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says. It introduces a source from the תורה.
To serve Him and to bless in His name (דברים י:ח)
One who serves, meaning a כהן doing the עבודה in the מקדש
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן may not do ברכת כהנים while drunk, but eating grape pits is fine. His rules come from the serving כהן in the מקדש ("לשרתו ולברך בשמו"), not from the full rules of a נזיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It fixes the exact limits of the drunk-כהן rule. Only real intoxication from wine blocks the blessing. Other grape products do not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said,
the verse says: "To serve Him and to bless in His name,"
phrases.notes: דברים 10:8. Serving and blessing appear together.

phrases.english: just as one who serves is permitted in grape pits,
so too a blessing kohen is permitted in grape pits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the grape-pits challenge of step 32 by bringing a verse that compares the blessing כהן to the serving כהן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New or refined scriptural source (comparison to the serving כהן instead of the נזיר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The blessing כהן is fully like a נזיר, so he would be forbidden even in grape pits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blessing כהן is like the serving כהן: forbidden when drunk on wine, permitted in grape pits.
